title: ITR Deadline: 31 October for Audited Accounts & Penalties

faq.q: Who exactly needs an audit for ITR filing?
faq.a: An audit is generally required for businesses with a turnover exceeding ₹1 crore, or professionals with gross receipts over ₹50 lakhs. Higher thresholds may apply under presumptive taxation schemes if certain conditions are met. Companies always require an audit.

faq.q: What happens if I file a belated return after 31 October?
faq.a: If you miss the 31 October deadline, you can still file a "belated return" generally until 31 December of the assessment year (i.e., 31 December 2026 for FY 2025-26). However, this will incur a late filing fee under Section 234F and interest under Section 234A, if applicable.

faq.q: Can I revise my ITR if I make a mistake after filing by 31 October?
faq.a: Yes, if you discover an error or omission after filing your original return, you can file a "revised return" under Section 139(5). This can generally be done until 31 December of the assessment year (31 December 2026 for FY 2025-26) or before the completion of assessment, whichever is earlier.

faq.q: Is there any way to waive off the late filing fee or interest?
faq.a: Generally, no. The late filing fee and interest under Section 234A are mandatory if the return is not filed by the due date or tax is not paid on time. In rare, exceptional circumstances, the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) may allow condonation of delay, but this is not a common occurrence.

faq.q: What if I am a salaried employee, but my employer's accounts are audited?
faq.a: If you are a salaried employee and do not have any business or professional income that requires an audit, your ITR due date remains 31 July. The 31 October deadline applies to the entity whose accounts are audited, not necessarily its employees.

faq.q: How is the 1% interest under Section 234A calculated if I file on, say, 15 November?
faq.a: The interest is calculated for each month or part of a month. So, if you file on 15 November, it will be counted as one full month of delay (from 31 October to 30 November), and interest for that month will be charged. If you file on 1 December, it would be two months.
